frontMatter.title: Phase 07 evidence: Auto Run, Cue, delegation, group chat and durable workflow ownership (automation pair)

summary: Phase 07 carried automation through the managed admission built in phase 06, on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.0). Every Auto Run turn (desktop and maestro-cli host) carries a workflow, task, trigger, run and attempt lineage and is admitted per attempt at the real spawn sink; a Cue prompt, shell or CLI run is admitted per firing on the subscription owner, pipeline, event and target, with the shell command gated as its own sink and an unsupported route refused with no local fallback; a nested maestro-cli dispatch and a consult are children of the operation that dispatched them, bound under an intersected scope and stamped on the child process, with a read-only initiator never gaining a writable consult; group chat moderator, participant, synthesis, recovery and background turns are admitted on the room's lineage; and the CP-03 owner/epoch/fence contract is consumed durably (claimed once per run and attempt, persisted, re-claimed with the held values on retry and restart, fenced when the registry says so, held offline only when issued, and an unknown holder never read as a fence). All of it is exercised locally by deterministic tests over the real lease authority, the real context verifier and the real run layer with the policy table and the workflow registry as declared doubles. On the real pair nothing managed is admitted: the sibling endpoint daemon is unenrolled and its socket server dispatches no workflow operation and its runtime adapter refuses any delegation chain or workflow context, so an enrolled Maestro refuses every automation route explicitly (unavailable, naming CP-03) and nothing counts as a positive paired result. The labeled container run of the real endpoint with the 0.9.0 library at this HEAD is recorded below as failed-attempt evidence.

realPairRun.reading: Peer authentication works on Linux (the native peer module built and the daemon answered the real client), the 0.9.0 library loads and composes the host adapter and verifier under the real client, and every step is denied or unavailable because the daemon is unenrolled (CP-04) and no approval producer exists; zero leases were issued. The outcomes are identical to the phase 04 run; what is new is the library at this HEAD. The driver has no workflow or delegation step: the endpoint's socket server (apps/endpoint/src/ipc/server.ts) dispatches attachment, compatibility, model, execution, telemetry, noticeList and inbox and answers any other operation unsupported_capability after attach, so a workflow claim through endpointWorkflowOwnerPort against this daemon could only end not-attached today, and the runtime adapter (packages/runtime-adapter/src/endpoint.ts) denies context-mismatch for any delegation chain or workflow. The workflow and delegation halves of the pair are therefore proven refused on the Maestro side (host-adapter answers unavailable naming CP-03 before the endpoint is asked) and have no producer to be proven admitted against.

deterministicCoverage.doubles: The policy table and the workflow registry (workflows.test.ts, stateful, in the endpoint's shapes). Everything else is real: createLocalHostAuthority (the lease authority), createContextVerifier, the run layer (startTurn / runAgentTurn / the fake agent as a real child process), ProcessManager with node-pty and the logger mocked and a stub child spawner reporting a pid (spawnGroupChatAgent.test.ts), the real createManagedHostAdapter over the real createLocalEndpointClient against the in-repo fake endpoint daemon (host-adapter.test.ts, spawnGroupChatAgent.test.ts), createWorkflowOwnership over real files.
cases: Auto Run lineage (autorun-turns, autorun, useAgentExecution, useBatchProcessor, useGoalRunner, serveSpawn): one workflow per batch or goal run, one request per task or iteration under one run id, the effort retry as the next attempt under the same request, the chat spawn carrying none; the desktop sink claims the fence for a fence: null lineage per attempt and binds on the registry's fence, a carried fence is not re-claimed, a producer refusal is answered before the authority with nothing started and the reason on the spawn failure, a fenced owner denied and a lost answer unknown never a fence, an unowned answer refused by name, a chat turn and a standalone host never ask

Zero effect under Auto Run (07-07): an owner the registry fenced starts nothing and never reaches the authority (permission_denied, non-recoverable); a policy that flips between two attempts refuses the effort retry with no second process; a revocation while the turn runs stops the process (interrupted, no lease live, ended() names the reason); a blank triggerEventId or fencingToken is refused by the verifier naming the field before the authority is asked

Cue prompt (cue-run-router.managed, cue-process-lifecycle.managed, cue-standalone-engine, host-cue, spawn-authority, service): admitted per firing on owner, pipeline, event and target; managed yolo or full permission does not widen the broker scope; a queued firing and a retry reauthorize; the fence claimed per firing as the installation, the next firing re-claiming the held values, owner_unfenced as the run's denied / policy-denied; a hosting runtime's claim used instead of the engine's; an enrolled machine's bare Cue engine refused 'holds no managed standing'

Cue shell (cue-shell-executor, dispatch): the final substituted command, resources and local-or-remote target gated at the sink; an unsupported shell route refused with no local fallback; a lease withdrawn between admission and spawn refused at the gate with no pid bound; a context not bound by this host's verifier refused unauthenticated before the policy reader; an unknown answer is unknown / outcome-unknown with the run failed; a policy that flips to deny refuses the next firing after one admitted run

Nested dispatch and consults (delegation, dispatch (CLI), messageHandlers, useRemoteHandlers, useRemoteIntegration, agentStore, retryStore, serveSpawn, consults, cue-cli-executor): an invalid record refuses the dispatch (never anonymous); the record travels all three wire paths and the queued item, is bound at the sink as the dispatcher's child under intersectDelegationScope (never a fresh chat turn), the child record stamped on the process after the ceiling so a grandchild deepens the chain; a retried turn carries the same record, a user follow-up none; a managed initiator on a standalone runtime refused; a read-only initiator never gains a writable consult; a run holding the fence hands it to the courier whole over a stale wider engine env, a run holding none hands none, under management refused whole over the unsupported route; a retried firing on its own attempt; two firings each with their own record

Group chat and background (spawnGroupChatAgent, background-turns, groupchat/spawn): a room turn bound as the room child with the host's generation, run under the lease this manager minted and released on exit; four roles share one root and parent with their own requests and leases; a dispatch from a participant's shell bound one link deeper with the room still the root; a consult a chat turn of its own; a forged record in the agent's variables neither widens the binding nor reaches the process; a revoked consult lease stops the consult; a policy that flips after the moderator refuses the participant; a blank ownerEpoch refused before the authority and journaled; an escalating consult admitted on and stamped with the record it carries, not the planted one; on an enrolled desktop over the real adapter and client the room turn is refused unavailable naming 'a delegation chain of 2' and CP-03 with nothing spawned and the endpoint never asked an execution

Durable ownership (workflows, host-adapter, service): a first claim offers epoch 0 and a nonce and holds the RECEIPT's epoch and token; a restarted host re-offers the held values and is confirmed as the one owner; a replayed attempt holds one record; two installations contend and exactly one holds a fence at the end, the fenced one fenced again after restart; a fenced offline holder keeps nothing; offline holding is what the registry last confirmed and cannot be widened on the unreachable claim; an unknown holder is not an offline holder and reads no fence after restart until confirmed; queued claims behind a fenced one are fenced; no standing, no policy revision, no port and an endpoint serving no such operation (capability-unsupported, CP-03) are refused by name, nothing stripped
